GOP Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) on Friday fawned over President Donald Trump for calling Russian President Vladimir Putin his “friend,” stating on Fox News that the comment was a “masterstroke.”

Trump has been attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit this week in Shenzhen, China.

“Who is he? He’s my friend!” Trump said with a laugh when he went to shake hands with Putin, who is accused of war crimes connected to the ongoing invasion of Ukraine.

“It’s strength and it’s confidence,” said Lee during an appearance on “The Ingraham Angle” Friday. “He exudes confidence. When I saw that clip that you’re referring to, the moment I watched it, I thought that was a masterstroke. Absolutely brilliant.”

See Lee’s remarks below:

Trump then brought up allegations that Russia engaged in election interference during his 2016 campaign against former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, doubling down on his claims that nothing of the sort had occurred — despite formal investigations suggesting otherwise.

“I’ve been dealing with Putin during the fake ‘Russia, Russia, Russia’ hoax,” Trump said. “And to be honest, he was very nice about it. It was a rigged hoax, it was a hoax that was made up by the Democrats.”

“He does this all the time,” she said. “You know, ‘Hey, who’s this? This is my friend, Mike Lee.’ He says that to everybody. So he walks in, and Putin’s like, ‘What?’ What do you do? Like, and [Secretary of State Marco] Rubio said this really well.”

She continued, “Rubio said that you have to deal with people as people, before anything can get done. Rubio said that you have to deal with people as people, before anything can get done.”

Trump promised ahead of his 2024 re-election that he would end the Ukraine war within a day. Despite that not happening, and Republicans getting demolished in the midterms earlier this month, Lee had nothing but praise for Trump’s foreign relations strategy.

“If President Trump treated his foreign adversaries the way his domestic adversaries treat him, the consequences for the American people, for American national security, would be disastrous,” Lee said. “Fortunately, he does not.”
